name: Japan (since 1945)
summary: Post-war Japan: occupied by the Allies until 1952, then a democratic constitutional monarchy that became one of the world’s largest economies.

location.value: An island country in East Asia: four main islands and over 14,000 smaller ones; capital Tokyo.

terrain.value: About 75% mountainous and forested, so people and farms crowd the eastern coastal plains.

climate.source: Gordon, A Modern History of Japan (2003)

resources.value: Few natural resources; imports most energy and raw materials.
resources.source: Gordon, A Modern History of Japan (2003)

disasters.value: Earthquakes and tsunamis, including Kobe (1995) and the 2011 Tōhoku earthquake and Fukushima nuclear disaster.
disasters.source: Gordon, A Modern History of Japan (2003)

urbanisation.value: Greater Tokyo is the world’s largest metropolitan area.
urbanisation.source: Gordon, A Modern History of Japan (2003)

inequality.source: Gordon, A Modern History of Japan (2003)

governmentType.value: A parliamentary constitutional monarchy; the emperor is head of state, the prime minister heads the government.

keyRulers.value: Emperors Hirohito, Akihito and Naruhito; prime ministers such as Yoshida Shigeru and Abe Shinzō.
keyRulers.source: Gordon, A Modern History of Japan (2003)
